statements.subject: session
statements.description: A stateful interaction between a Client and a Broker. Some Sessions last only as long as the Network Connection; others can span multiple Network Connections.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client requests to connect to the Broker. This is the first packet sent by a Client.

actions: receive CONNACK with success return code

actions: receive CONNACK with error return code

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An AUTH Control Packet is sent from the Client to the Broker or from the Broker to the Client as part of an extended authentication exchange. The Authentication Method is set in the CONNECT packet, and consequent AUTH packets follow the same Authentication Method.
actions: exchange AUTH packet during extended authentication

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The DISCONNECT packet is the final MQTT Control Packet sent from the Client or the Broker. It indicates the reason why the Network Connection is being closed.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the Network Connection is closed without the Client first sending a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x00 (Normal disconnection) and the MQTT Connection has a Will Message, the Will Message is published.
statements.trigger: Network Connection closed without Normal disconnection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the Network Connection is not closed normally, the Broker sends a last Will Message for the Client if the Client provided one in its CONNECT packet. Situations include: an I/O error or network failure detected by the Broker; the Client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive period; the Client closes the Network Connection without first sending a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x00; the Broker closes the Network Connection without first receiving a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x00.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the Will Flag is set in the CONNECT flags, then the Payload of the CONNECT packet includes information about the Will. The information consists of the Will Properties, Will Topic, and Will Payload fields.
statements.guard_semantics: connection.will_flag = true → CONNECT.payload includes Will Properties, Will Topic, Will Payload

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Step (A): Client sends Token request to the Authorization Server before initiating an MQTT connection.
actions: send Token request to Authorization Server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Step (B): Authorization Server returns Access token to Client in response to token request.
actions: receive Access token from Authorization Server

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step (C): Client sends Connection request along with the access token to the Broker, initiating connection setup.
actions: send Connection request with access token to Broker

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Step (D): Broker optionally sends Introspection request to the Authorization Server to validate the access token presented by the Client.
actions: send Introspection request to Authorization Server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Step (E): Authorization Server optionally sends Introspection response to Broker, completing token validation.
actions: receive Introspection response from Authorization Server

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Step (F): Broker sends Connection response to Client, completing connection setup.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client holds an access token obtained from the Authorization Server and is ready to initiate an MQTT connection request to the Broker.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client has sent Connection request with access token to Broker and is awaiting Connection response; Broker may optionally perform introspection during this state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Broker has sent Introspection request to Authorization Server and is awaiting Introspection response before proceeding with connection authorization.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client has received Connection response from Broker; connection setup is complete and the Client may use the Pub/Sub interface.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Connection request sent by the Client to the Broker (step C) must include the access token obtained from the Authorization Server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST authenticate to the Broker either over MQTT or TLS before performing any other action.
actions: authenticate to broker over MQTT or TLS

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The token is transported inside the CONNECT packet and MUST be validated using one of the methods described in Section 2.2.2 (TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The token is transported inside the CONNECT packet (for TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace option).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the Client uses TLS:Anon,MQTT:None, the Client can only publish or subscribe to public topics.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST authenticate the Broker during the TLS handshake.
actions: validate broker public key or certificate against rs_cnf parameter

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Client connects to the Broker to publish its token to the 'authz-info' topic using the TLS:Anon,MQTT:None option over a TLS connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: After publishing the token, the Client disconnects from the Broker.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Client is expected to reconnect using client authentication over TLS (i.e., TLS:Known(RPK/PSK),MQTT:none).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client connects to the Broker to publish its token to the 'authz-info' topic, using the TLS:Anon,MQTT:None option over a TLS connection.
actions: establish TLS connection with anonymous credentials

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After publishing the token, the Client disconnects from the Broker.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client is expected to reconnect using client authentication over TLS (i.e., TLS:Known(RPK/PSK),MQTT:none).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST verify the validity of the token. If the token is not valid, the Broker MUST discard the token.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker stores and indexes all tokens received to the 'authz-info' topic in its key store.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the QoS level is equal to 0, and the token is not valid, or if the claims cannot be obtained in the case of an introspected token, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized).
statements.trigger: token validation failure on authz-info PUBLISH (QoS=0)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the PUBLISH Payload does not parse to a token, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT with reason code 0x99 (Payload format invalid).
statements.trigger: payload parse failure on authz-info PUBLISH (QoS=0)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the QoS level of the PUBLISH packet is greater than or equal to 1, and the token is not valid, or the claims cannot be obtained in the case of an introspected token, the Broker MUST send reason code 0x87 (Not authorized) in the PUBACK or PUBREC.
statements.trigger: token validation failure on authz-info PUBLISH (QoS>=1)
actions: send PUBACK or PUBREC with reason code 0x87

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the PUBLISH Payload does not parse to a token, the PUBACK/PUBREC reason code is 0x99 (Payload format invalid).
statements.trigger: payload parse failure on authz-info PUBLISH (QoS>=1)
actions: send PUBACK or PUBREC with reason code 0x99

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The 'authz-info' topic MUST only be published (i.e., the Clients are not allowed to subscribe to it).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After sending the CONNECT packet, the Client MUST wait to receive the CONNACK packet from the Broker. The only packets it is allowed to send are DISCONNECT or AUTH that are in response to the Broker AUTH.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Except for a DISCONNECT and AUTH response from the Client, the Broker MUST NOT process any packets before sending a CONNACK packet.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After sending the CONNECT packet, the Client MUST wait to receive the CONNACK packet from the Broker.
actions: send CONNECT packet with token in Authentication Data

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The only packets it is allowed to send are DISCONNECT or AUTH that are in response to the Broker AUTH.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Broker MUST check that the token allows the publication of the Will Message. If the Will authorization fails, the connection is refused.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In MQTT v5.0, the Client signals a new Session by setting the Clean Start flag to 1 in the CONNECT packet. If the Broker starts a new Session, the Broker MUST set the Session Present flag to 0 in the CONNACK packet to signal this to the Client.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a CONNECT packet is received with Clean Start set to 0, and there is a Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Broker MUST resume communications with the Client based on the state from the existing Session. The Broker MUST set the Session Present flag to 1 in the CONNACK packet.
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with Clean Start = 0 and existing session

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If this Client Identifier represents a Client already connected to the Broker, the Broker sends a DISCONNECT packet to the existing Client with reason code 0x8E (Session taken over) and closes the connection to the Client.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The User Name Flag and Password Flag MUST be set to 0 to use AUTH packets for authentication and authorization.
statements.guard_semantics: must be 0 when using AUTH-based token transport

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The User Name Flag and Password Flag MUST be set to 0 to use AUTH packets for authentication and authorization.
statements.guard_semantics: must be 0 when using AUTH-based token transport

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When reconnecting to a Broker that supports continuing existing Sessions, the Client MUST still provide a token in addition to using the same Client Identifier and setting the Clean Start to 0.
statements.guard_semantics: must be present even when resuming an existing session (connect.clean_start = 0)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as a property of a CONNECT packet by using the property identifier 21 (0x15), which MUST be set to "ace".

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Authentication Method is followed by the Authentication Data, which has a property identifier 22 (0x16) and is Binary Data.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Broker does not support this profile, it sends a CONNACK packet with reason code 0x8C (Bad authentication method).
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with unsupported authentication profile
actions: send CONNACK with reason code 0x8C (Bad authentication method)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The token is also validated, as described in Section 2.2.5, and the Broker responds with a CONNACK packet with the appropriate response code.
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with PoP Authentication Data (token length, token, MAC or signature over TLS exporter content)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Authentication Data inside the Client's CONNECT packet MUST contain the two-byte integer token length, the token, and the keyed message digest (MAC) or the Client signature.
allowed_values: MAC or Client signature over TLS exporter content

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client cannot reauthenticate using this method during the same TLS session.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Authentication Data inside the Client's CONNECT contains only the two-byte integer token length and the token, the Broker MUST respond with an AUTH packet with the authenticated reason code set to 0x18 (Continue Authentication).
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with token-only Authentication Data
actions: send AUTH reason_code=0x18 with 8-byte RS nonce as challenge

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker also uses this method if the Authentication Data does not contain a token, but the Broker has a token stored for the connecting Client.
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with no token but stored token exists for client
actions: send AUTH reason_code=0x18 with 8-byte RS nonce as challenge

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client responds to this with an AUTH packet with reason code 0x18 (Continue Authentication). The Authentication Data includes the 8-byte Client nonce and the signature or MAC computed over the RS nonce concatenated with the Client nonce using PoP key in the token.
statements.trigger: AUTH 0x18 received from Broker with RS nonce challenge
actions: send AUTH reason_code=0x18 with client_nonce and MAC_or_signature over (rs_nonce || client_nonce)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Next, the token is validated. The success case is illustrated in Figure 7: after token validation the Broker sends CONNACK 0x00 (Success).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker continues authentication using an AUTH packet that contains the Authentication Method and the Authentication Data. The Authentication Method MUST be set to 'ace', and the Authentication Data MUST NOT be empty and MUST contain an 8-byte RS nonce as a challenge for the Client.
statements.trigger: AUTH 0x18 received from Client with client nonce and MAC

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker continues authentication; AUTH 0x18 (Continue Authentication) with RS nonce challenge has been sent and Broker is awaiting the client's challenge response.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker is performing token validation after receiving the client's AUTH 0x18 challenge response (may involve introspection).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Authentication Method MUST be set to 'ace' in the Broker's AUTH challenge packet during PoP challenge/response.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Authentication Data MUST NOT be empty and MUST contain an 8-byte RS nonce as a challenge for the Client in the Broker's AUTH packet.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MAY also reauthenticate using this challenge-response flow, as described in Section 4.
statements.trigger: client initiates reauthentication via PoP challenge-response
actions: send AUTH to initiate PoP reauthentication

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST verify the validity of the token either locally or MAY send a request to the introspection endpoint of the AS. The Broker MUST verify the claims in the access token.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Validation of the signature or MAC MUST fail if the signature algorithm is set to 'none' when the key used for the signature algorithm cannot be determined or the computed and received signature/MAC do not match.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST check if the access token is still valid, if it is the intended destination (i.e., the audience) of the token, and if the token was issued by an authorized Authorization Server.
statements.pre_cond: token.valid = false | token.audience != broker.id | token.issuer_authorized = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker validates the signature or the MAC, depending on how the PoP protocol is implemented, to authenticate the Client.
statements.pre_cond: token.valid = true & token.audience = broker.id & token.issuer_authorized = true & token.signature_valid = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The 'cnf' claim MUST contain either the Client's RPK or, if the key is already known by the Broker (e.g., from previous communication), a reference to it.
statements.guard_semantics: required when Client uses TLS RPK mode to authenticate to Broker

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The token or its introspection result MUST be cached to allow a Client's future PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: During the CONNECT, if the Will Flag is set to 1, the Broker MUST also authorize the publication of the Will Topic and Will Message using the token's scope field.
actions: authorize Will Topic and Will Message using token scope field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY signal in the CONNACK explicitly whether Wildcard Subscriptions are supported by returning a CONNACK property 'Wildcard Subscription Available'.
actions: send CONNACK with Wildcard Subscription Available property

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the scope is empty, the Broker records no permissions for the Client for any topic. In this case, the Client is not able to publish or subscribe to any protected topics.
actions: record no topic permissions for client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The non-empty scope is used to authorize the Will Topic, if provided, in the CONNECT packet, during connection setup and, if the connection request succeeds, the Topic Names or Topic Filters requested in the future PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packets.
statements.trigger: connection request succeeds & scope is non-empty
actions: authorize future PUBLISH Topic Names using scope
authorize future SUBSCRIBE Topic Filters using scope

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For the authorization to succeed, the Broker MUST verify that the Topic Name or Topic Filter in question is either an exact match to or a subset of at least one topic_filter in the scope.
actions: verify Topic Name or Topic Filter is exact match or subset of at least one scope topic_filter

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Based on the validation result (obtained either via local inspection or using the introspection interface of the AS), the Broker MUST send a CONNACK packet to the Client.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Authentication can fail for the following reasons: if the Client does not provide a valid token, the Client omits the Authentication Data field and the Broker has no token stored for the Client, the token or Authentication data are malformed, or if the Will Flag is set, the authorization checks for the Will Topic fails. The Broker responds with the CONNACK reason code 0x87 (Not Authorized) or any other applicable reason code.
statements.pre_cond: client.token_valid = false | (client.authentication_data_present = false & server.stored_token = null) | client.token_malformed = true | (connection.will_flag = true & will_topic.authorized = false)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY also trigger AS discovery and include a User Property (identified as property type 38 (0x26)) in the CONNACK for the AS Request Creation Hints.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The name of the User Property MUST be set to 'ace_as_hint' when the Broker includes AS Request Creation Hints in the CONNACK.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On success, the reason code of the CONNACK is 0x00 (Success). Having accepted the connection, the Broker MUST be prepared to store the token during the connection and after disconnection for future use.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Broker starts a new Session, it MUST also set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet to signal a new Session to the Client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, it MUST set Session Present to 1 in the CONNACK packet.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The reason code of the CONNACK is 0x00 (Success) on authorization success; Session Present must be set to 0 for new session or 1 for existing session.
statements.guard_semantics: 0 if session.is_new = true; 1 if session.is_new = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Having accepted the connection, the Broker MUST be prepared to store the token during the connection and after disconnection for future use. PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packets, which are sent after a connection setup, do not contain access tokens.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the token is not self-contained and the Broker uses token introspection, it MAY cache the validation result to authorize the subsequent PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packets.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Client is allowed to publish to the topic, the Broker publishes the message to all valid subscribers of the topic.
actions: publish message to all valid subscribers of the topic

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of an authorization failure, the Broker MUST return an error if the Client has set the QoS level of the PUBLISH packet to greater than or equal to 1. Depending on the QoS level, the Broker responds with either a PUBACK or PUBREC packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized).
actions: send PUBACK with reason_code=0x87 if QoS=1
send PUBREC with reason_code=0x87 if QoS=2

statements.subject: client
statements.description: On receiving an acknowledgment with 0x87 (Not authorized), the Client MAY reauthenticate by providing a new token.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: For QoS level 0, the Broker sends a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized) and closes the Network Connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker sends a DISCONNECT packet and closes the Network Connection on authorization failure for QoS 0.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For all QoS levels, the Broker MAY return 0x80 (Unspecified error) if they do not want to leak the Topic Names to unauthorized clients.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker MUST close the Network Connection and SHOULD send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized) before closing the Network Connection to unauthorized subscribers.
statements.trigger: Unauthorized subscriber identified for PUBLISH forwarding
actions: send DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Broker forwards the PUBLISH packet to all the valid subscribers — subscribers with valid matching Topic Subscriptions and authorized access.
statements.trigger: PUBLISH packet received with valid matching Topic Subscription and authorized subscriber

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On receiving the SUBSCRIBE packet, the Broker MUST use the type of packet (i.e., SUBSCRIBE) and the Topic Filter in the packet header to match against the scope field of the stored token or introspection result.
actions: match Topic Filter against scope field of stored token or introspection result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As a response to the SUBSCRIBE packet, the Broker issues a SUBACK packet. For each Topic Filter, the SUBACK packet includes a return code matching the QoS level for the corresponding Topic Filter.
actions: send SUBACK with QoS return code for each authorized Topic Filter

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of failure, the return code is 0x87, indicating that the Client is not authorized.
actions: send SUBACK with return code 0x87 (Not Authorized) for each unauthorized Topic Filter

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY return 0x80 (Unspecified error) if they do not want to leak the Topic Names to unauthorized clients.
actions: send SUBACK with return code 0x80 (Unspecified Error) instead of 0x87

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A reason code is returned for each Topic Filter. Therefore, the Client may receive success codes for a subset of its Topic Filters while being unauthorized for the rest.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: After sending a DISCONNECT packet, the Network Connection is closed, and no more messages can be sent.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: To start reauthentication, the Client MUST send an AUTH packet with reason code 0x19 (Reauthentication).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST check for token expiration whenever a CONNECT, PUBLISH, or SUBSCRIBE packet is received or sent.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Token expirations may trigger the Broker to send PUBACK, SUBACK, and DISCONNECT packets with the return code set to 'Not authorized'. After sending a DISCONNECT packet, the Network Connection is closed, and no more messages can be sent.
actions: send DISCONNECT with return code 'Not authorized'

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To start reauthentication, the Client MUST send an AUTH packet with reason code 0x19 (Reauthentication). The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as 'ace' and transport the new token in the Authentication Data.
actions: transport new token in Authentication Data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker accepts reauthentication requests if the Client has already submitted a token (may be expired), for which it performed proof of possession. Otherwise, the Broker MUST deny the request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the reauthentication fails, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not Authorized).
actions: send DISCONNECT with reason code 0x87 (Not Authorized)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as 'ace' and transport the new token in the Authentication Data.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as 'ace' and transport the new token in the Authentication Data.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: if the Session is currently not connected, the time at which the Session will end and the Session State will be discarded.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: if the Session Expiry Interval is set to 0, the Broker doesn't store the Session State but MUST keep the retained messages.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Broker stores the Session State, the state MAY include the token and its introspection result (for reference tokens) in addition to the MQTT Session State.
actions: optionally store token and introspection result

statements.subject: session
statements.description: if the Session is currently not connected, the time at which the Session will end and the Session State will be discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In case of disconnections due to network errors or server disconnection due to a protocol error (which includes authorization errors), the Will Message is sent if the Client supplied a Will in the CONNECT packet. The Will Message MUST be published to the Will Topic, regardless of whether the corresponding token has expired.
actions: publish Will Message to Will Topic regardless of token expiry

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The messages to be retained are indicated to the Broker by setting a RETAIN flag in a PUBLISH packet. This way, the publisher signals to the Broker to store the most recent message for the associated topic.
statements.guard_semantics: RETAIN=1 triggers broker to store most recent message for associated topic

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client's token scope array MUST include the Will Topic.
statements.guard_semantics: token.scope includes Will Topic; required pre-condition for Will Message publication

statements.subject: message
statements.description: the Broker MUST use the minimum of the token expiry and message expiry interval to discard a retained message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Broker MUST continue publishing the retained messages as long as the associated tokens are valid.
actions: publish retained message to new subscriber

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Brokers that do not support MQTT v3.1.1 Clients return a CONNACK packet with reason code 0x84 (Unsupported Protocol Version) in response to the connection requests.
actions: send CONNACK with reason code 0x84 (Unsupported Protocol Version)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If there is no Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Broker MUST create a new Session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Clean flag is set to 0, the Broker MUST resume communications with the Client based on the state from the current Session (as identified by the Client Identifier).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Client SHOULD set the Clean flag to 1 to always start a new Session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Clean flag is set to 0, the Broker MUST resume communications with the Client based on the state from the current Session.
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with Clean flag = 0 and existing session

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If there is no Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Broker MUST create a new Session.
statements.trigger: CONNECT received with Clean flag = 0 and no existing session

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker MUST set the Session Present flag in the CONNACK packet accordingly, i.e., 0 to indicate a new Session to the Client and 1 to indicate that the existing Session is continued.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker MUST set the Session Present flag in the CONNACK packet accordingly, i.e., 1 to indicate that the existing Session is continued.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the Client provided the token via the 'authz-info' topic and will not update the token in the CONNECT packet, it MUST authenticate over TLS. The subsequent TLS handshake would fail without a valid token.
statements.trigger: token published to authz-info topic without CONNECT token update

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Broker MUST still perform PoP validation on the provided Client token.
actions: perform PoP validation on Client token

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: User Name and Password flags MUST be set to 1 to ensure that the Payload of the CONNECT packet includes both the User Name and Password fields.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: User Name and Password flags MUST be set to 1 to ensure that the Payload of the CONNECT packet includes both the User Name and Password fields.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The tokenless CONNECT attempt MUST fail. The challenge-response-based PoP is not possible for MQTT v3.1.1.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the case of an authorization error, the Broker MUST ignore the PUBLISH packet and disconnect the Client.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Token expirations MUST lead to disconnecting the Client rather than silently dropping messages when the Broker is forwarding PUBLISH packets to subscribed Clients.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Broker will disconnect on almost any error and may not keep the Session State, necessitating that clients make a greater effort to ensure that tokens remain valid.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After the Broker validates an access token and accepts a connection from a client, it caches the token to authorize a Client's publish and subscribe requests in an ongoing Session.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: After the Broker validates an access token and accepts a connection from a client, it caches the token to authorize a Client's publish and subscribe requests in an ongoing Session.
statements.trigger: access token validated and connection accepted

statements.subject: session
statements.description: For MQTT v5.0, when a Client connects with a long Session Expiry Interval, the Broker may need to maintain the Client's MQTT Session State after it disconnects for an extended period.
statements.trigger: Client disconnects with long Session Expiry Interval

statements.subject: session
statements.description: For MQTT v3.1.1, the Session State may need to be stored indefinitely, as it does not have a Session Expiry Interval feature.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Broker caches the token introspection responses, then the Broker SHOULD use a reasonable cache timeout to introspect tokens regularly.
